A Firestore engineer disputed Convex's comparison article. They said its claim that Firestore results from separate queries won't stay in sync is incorrect, because Firestore does provide global consistency. Stale cached data only happens if you explicitly opt in while offline.

A commenter asked whether Convex's reactivity is just smart polling. They noted that Firestore sends incremental updates by broadcasting individual documents as commits happen, whereas Convex reruns the whole query when its read set overlaps with a mutation.

Praise for Convex's design: "I like the model of the full function becomes the point of reactivity." It is very different from Firestore, which syncs data to the device. Firestore gets better offline behavior from local cached queries, but remote execution has its own benefits. "I do think this is a super cool product!"

Responding to the Convex author's claim that Supabase, like Firebase, lacks server-side reactivity and pushes SQL queries to the client, a user countered that you can put that logic on the server with Postgres views in Supabase. Another user added that Supabase also offers RPC functions.
